subject: ClearGate: RCA, timeline and follow-up commitments
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@cleargate.com>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@cleargate.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ClearGate: RCA, timeline and follow-up commitments

Alex / Sara,

Thanks again for your patience while we finished the internal review. Attached is our final RCA for the April 9th inference availability degradation (attached: ClearGate_RCA_Apr2028.pdf). Below is a short, customer-facing summary and the concrete follow-ups we will deliver.

Executive summary (short):
- What happened: A software rollback of a router-side optimization caused intermittent KV-cache invalidation under specific tokenization patterns, which resulted in elevated tail latency for a subset of ClearGate requests between 02:34–03:21 UTC on Apr 9.
- Impact: ~0.9% of requests experienced >5s tail latency; 0.1% saw transient failures (5xx). No data loss or model corruption.
- Root cause: The rollback changed an internal cache-bump ordering when the token stream contained long contiguous separators; a race condition allowed stale cache pointers to be used.

Timeline (high level):
- 2028-04-09 02:29 UTC — First alert: elevated 99.9th percentile latency on region-us-1 for model-rw-16b.
- 2028-04-09 02:34 UTC — Interruption window begins; automated routing to fallback model-tier slowed due to an unrelated autoscaler limit.
- 2028-04-09 03:12 UTC — Engineering rollback and targeted routing change applied; degradation reduced.
- 2028-04-09 03:21 UTC — Metrics stabilized and error rates returned to baseline.

Customer commitments we will deliver within the next two weeks:
1) Clear RCA doc (attached) with code references and timeline — delivered (this attachment).
2) A patch to the router ordering logic with tests — planned release 2028-04-18.
3) A config guard that prevents autoscaler conflicts for fallback routing — planned 2028-04-20.
4) A tailored runbook for handling similar degradations and a 30-minute on-call war-room playbook — attached (inference-runbook-v1.md) and final by 2028-04-20.
5) SLO credit consideration: we will follow up with proposed credit terms after internal review (target by Apr 13).

I've included Marissa and Hannah on this message for any operational or compensation questions. If you'd like a short call to walk through the RCA, I'm available tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ClearGate_RCA_Apr2028.pdf (PDF, 42 pages), inference-runbook-v1.md (text)
From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@cleargate.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@cleargate.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 09:45:22 -0700
Subject: Re: ClearGate: RCA, timeline and follow-up commitments

Camila,

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the detailed write-up — appreciate the clear timeline. A couple quick items from our side:

- Thanks for the confirmation that there was no data loss. That's the most important.
- We'd like to schedule a 30-minute walk-through of the RCA with your engineering lead. Tomorrow afternoon PST works for us.
- On SLO credits: given the customer impact, we're expecting a credit proposal that reflects the customer-run costs and the operational disruption. Please include an explicit credit amount in your follow-up so we can route internally.

Sara — I'll coordinate with you on availability.

Alex
Director of Platform Ops
ClearGate Payments

Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: ClearGate: RCA, timeline and follow-up commitments — SLO credit request

Team — forwarding Alex's note. He explicitly requested a proposed credit amount to present to procurement. Wanted to align on the proposal before sending it back.

Key context:
- Impact window: ~47 minutes total with measurable client-side retries and a small % of failures.
- Customer importance: production payments processing, high-touch.
- Contract: ClearGate is on our Enterprise Standard plan with a 99.9% availability SLO for inference for this account (see deal DEAL-4872).

Proposed options (for quick decision):
A) Symmetric: 5% monthly credit for the month of April on net usage (simple, fast).
B) Tiered: credit proportional to observed request failure fraction — equivalent to 10% of the prorated uptime loss in April. This requires a short calculation but is more exact.
C) Operational: 2 weeks of committed priority response time plus a 3% one-time credit.

Preference: I'd recommend Option B (accurate), but if we need speed to preserve the relationship Option A gets put through quickly.

Thoughts? If you approve, I'll send the credit proposal to Alex and Sara and schedule the RCA walk-through with our engineering lead (requesting 30 minutes tomorrow afternoon PST).

Thanks,
Camila

Camila — thanks for laying out options. I agree with Option B where possible; we should calculate the credit precisely to show good faith and avoid over/under compensation. Action items:
- Marissa: I'll run a quick usage delta on ClearGate's Apr bill vs baseline and compute the prorated uptime loss (2 hours window considered) — deliverable by Apr 13 EOD.
- Hannah: please coordinate with engineering on the patch release ETA and confirm the post-deploy verification steps. Need the runbook checked for any missing fallbacks.
- Camila: once we have the numbers, send a one-time credit proposal and the scheduling link for the RCA walkthrough.

Also — include legal if the credit is >7% so procurement can pre-clear.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: ClearGate: RCA walk-through scheduled and credit proposal

Alex / Sara,

Thanks for the call earlier — appreciated the constructive feedback. Per our internal analysis (see attached RCA), we propose the following credit approach for April 2028:

Credit calculation summary:
- Observed error window: 2028-04-09 02:34–03:21 UTC (47 minutes)
- Estimated effective impact on production: 0.9% of total requests had elevated tail latency; 0.1% observed transient failures
- Prorated credit: Using Option B methodology, we prorated the SLA loss across April and propose a one-time 4.6% credit on April net inference usage, capped at 8% per contract threshold.

Deliverables and timelines (confirmed):
- Router ordering patch (with UTs & e2e checks) — release 2028-04-18 (Hannah leading).
- Autoscaler guard for fallback routing — 2028-04-20 (Hannah + infra).
- Finalized runbook and verification playbook — 2028-04-20.
- RCA note with code refs and metric links — attached and posted to Drive.

Next steps for us:
- Camila to send a formal credit memo (PDF) to procurement and confirm acceptance.
- Marissa to finalize the credit calculation numbers and confirm cap with Legal if >7%.
- Hannah to confirm post-deploy checks and share test results in the runbook.

Please reply to confirm you'd like the credit memo as a DocuSign or as a standard invoice adjustment. We'll start the procurement flow immediately after your confirmation.

Best regards,
Camila Reyes
Account Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
